source.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
source.authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran; Yue Zhao; Armin W. Thomas; E. Adeli; Jia-Jun Wu; Juan Carlos Niebles; Fei-Fei Li; Michael Poli

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures validation token NLL across image-model sizes, which bears conceptually on scaling in another modality, but it does not fit or test a power law.
record.gate_note: Figure 7 and its accompanying text report image- and text-token validation NLL decreasing with Halcyon model size. Only the image-token result is recorded for V5; the figure does not provide extractable numeric values, and the text does not establish a power-law form. The reported gFD and benchmark scores are generation-quality measures, not held-out cross-entropy. Results in Tables 6–9 concern pretraining composition and captioning, not power-law scaling.
record.test_reason: In an image-text autoregressive setting, the paper reports that held-out image-token NLL falls with model size (0.1B–4B; Figure 7, Table 9). That bears on V5, but nothing is fitted, so whether the curve follows a power law is not shown. Scaling is a side result; the paper's main question is whether language pretraining is needed.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that strong T2I models can be trained from scratch on paired image–text data without internet-scale language pretraining, and that text-only pretraining does not help. They note in passing that NLL and gFD improve with size, but make no power-law claim.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales from-scratch multimodal image-generation models and reports validation NLL; it does not reproduce the original language-model scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size is varied from 0.1B to 4B; the reported image-token validation NLL decreases with size.

fits_no_version.finding: Image generation quality improves with Halcyon size. gFD falls 144.2→72.6→48.0→35.3→28.4 and GenEval rises 27.3→56.4. DPG-Bench plateaus at 77.9 for both 1.6B and 4B (Tables 4, 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream image-generation metrics improve monotonically with model size in from-scratch multimodal AR models, with possible saturation on some benchmarks.

fits_no_version.finding: Caption text-token NLL(T|∅) falls with size, 1.601→1.338 (Table 9), in a multimodal model trained only on captions, not a text language model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Text-token loss in multimodal early-fusion models decreases with model size.

record.problems: The image-token NLL result is shown only in a figure, with no extractable numeric values or uncertainty reported for that measure. The size range is 0.1B to 4B, and the paper does not fit a power law or test extrapolation.

untested.parts: Power-law form and exponents for image-token loss; scaling in data or compute (tokens fixed at one epoch); video, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer.
Not tested; no text-only language model scaling.
Not tested; no extrapolation from fits.
Not tested; no compute-optimal allocation sweep.
Not tested; no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Not tested for language models; no predictability analysis.

missing.what: Final test NLL(I|T) and NLL(I|∅) per model size (0.1B–4B), the numeric form of the r1 trend
Total pretraining FLOPs per Halcyon size (2.05e20 to 3.08e21), needed to plot loss against compute

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is given: the only linked evidence is a monotone loss decrease, and the version's core claim (power-law form) is not testable from five unfitted points. Per-log-size NLL drops shrink (~0.24, 0.20, 0.12, 0.12 per unit ln N), consistent with a power law plus offset, but this is my reading, not the authors'. The training-seed std at 0.1B is 5.54 gFD; no NLL uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: No test of power-law held-out pretraining loss in language models across parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits or predictions evaluated on substantially larger runs.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.

The paper reports only a qualitative decrease in image-token validation NLL with model size; it does not fit a power law or estimate exponents. It covers one image-generation setup and does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The paper reports image-generation benchmark scores by model size, but does not test predictability of downstream-task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
No analysis of scaling-law fit choices, exponent variation, or curves bending away from a single power law.

rows.subject: Halcyon (0.1B, 0.25B, 0.52B, 1.6B, and 4B; aggregate size sweep)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained from scratch on GPIC; validation during pretraining
rows.operation_detail: Compared image-token validation NLL across five model sizes during pretraining.
rows.note: Recorded as one aggregate size sweep because the text describes the trend across all five sizes, while the figure values are not extractable here. The paper states that image NLL decreases consistently with size, but this does not determine whether the relationship is a power law.
rows.check: The value is not figure-only. Table 9 gives final GPIC Test-50K NLL(I|T) by size: 8.727, 8.509, 8.366, 8.235, 8.122 (0.1B→4B). NLL(I|∅) is 8.774→8.193. The decrease is monotone with shrinking gains per log-size, but five points with no fit and no irreducible term cannot establish power-law form. All sizes train on the same one epoch (~102B image tokens), so data may be a bottleneck for the larger models. The state stays cannot_determine; the value should be filled from Table 9.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
